title: Unsupervised machine learning identifies five heart failure subtypes across EHR sources
summary: Four unsupervised clustering methods applied to 87 factors in primary-care records identified five heart failure subtypes (early-onset, late-onset, AF-related, metabolic, cardiometabolic) in CPRD (188,799 cases) and THIN (124,263 cases). Subtypes were similar across datasets, differed in one-year mortality and other outcomes, and showed genetic associations in UK Biobank (9,573 cases). The subtype labels are descriptive and the data retrospective; preprint of 2022-06-28.
ai_technology: Unsupervised clustering (K-means, hierarchical, K-medoids, mixture model) on electronic health record factors
organization: University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust; Barts Health NHS Trust; UCL Biomedical Research Centre

evidence.tested: External validity across CPRD and THIN, prognostic validity for one-year mortality, and genetic validity in UK Biobank.
evidence.unknown: Whether subtypes change management or trial design is not shown; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Unsupervised machine learning clustered patients into candidate heart failure subtypes.
